question:
A “stair-step” figure is made up of alternating shaded and unshaded squares in each row. Rows \(1\) through \(4\) are shown. All rows begin and end with an unshaded square. The number of shaded squares in the \(37\)th row is

[Figure 1](figures/1985_AMC_8_Q07_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The diagram shows rows of \(1,3,5,7\) squares: each step down makes the row two squares longer. Because every row starts unshaded and alternates, it consists of one initial unshaded square followed by shaded-unshaded pairs.

Each step down adds one such pair. Row \(1\) has no pairs, so row \(n\), for a positive integer \(n\), has \(n-1\) pairs. Each pair contains exactly one shaded square, and every shaded square belongs to one pair. Therefore, row \(37\) contains
\[
37-1=36
\]
shaded squares, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

reference.solution:
Method 1: Count shaded-unshaded pairs

The diagram shows rows of \(1,3,5,7\) squares: each step down makes the row two squares longer. Because every row starts unshaded and alternates, it consists of one initial unshaded square followed by shaded-unshaded pairs.

Each step down adds one such pair. Row \(1\) has no pairs, so row \(n\), for a positive integer \(n\), has \(n-1\) pairs. Each pair contains exactly one shaded square, and every shaded square belongs to one pair. Therefore, row \(37\) contains
\[
37-1=36
\]
shaded squares, choice \(\boxed{\text{C}}\).

nodes.description: Write simple expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them. For example, express the calculation “add 8 and 7, then multiply by 2” as 2 × (8 + 7). Recognize that 3 × (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921, without having to calculate the indicated sum or product.
